key_insight: ToolPrivacyBench shows that an LLM agent can complete a multi-tool task correctly while still over-sharing private data across tool calls, so privacy must be evaluated at the trajectory level, not just by final output.
engineering_relevance: For tool-using AI systems, this benchmark highlights the need for need-to-know data routing, tool-specific access control, and audit logging to prevent unnecessary privacy leakage in production agents.
method: Builds a benchmark of privacy-sensitive multi-tool workflows with policy knowledge bases.
Checks tool arguments and backend audit logs against authorized purpose-bound disclosures.
Audits nine common agents for privacy over-disclosure during executed tool trajectories.
evidence_signal: The benchmark contains 2,150 cases, including 1,150 synthetic workflows and 1,000 adapted multi-tool/function-calling cases, and evaluates agents by comparing tool calls and backend logs to policy rules.
watch_item: Because the benchmark relies on mock backends and predefined policy knowledge bases, real-world deployment may still require adapting the auditing rules to more complex or ambiguous enterprise workflows.
paper_title: ToolPrivacyBench: Benchmarking Purpose-Bound Privacy in Tool-Using LLM Agents
